mha.d: Attention with \( H \) heads in which each head has its own query, key and value projections. In the KV cache, it stores \( H \times (d_k + d_v) \) numbers per token and per layer, or \( 2 \times H \times d_h \) when key and value have the same size \( d_h \).

mqa.d: Variant in which all query heads share a single key and value head: the KV shrinks by a factor of \( H \). The sparse indexers are MQA, and MLA during decode becomes an MQA over the latent. Under tensor parallel, the single head is replicated on every rank.

gqa.d: Middle ground between MHA and MQA: the \( H \) query heads form \( G \) groups that share K and V. Kernels require \( H \) to be a multiple of \( G \) (qo % kv == 0), and any padding for TP has to keep the ratio. E.g.: Qwen3.8 24:2; DFlash2 drafter 32:8 (36:9 at TP3).

razao-de-grupo.d: Number of query heads per K/V head, \( H/G \). Each KV row read from memory serves that many queries. Any head padding has to preserve it so as not to remap queries onto the wrong keys.

mla.d: Attention in which the K and V of every head are derived from one compressed latent per token (kv_lora_rank, 512 in DeepSeek and GLM), and only that latent goes into the cache. With weight absorption, decode becomes an MQA over the latent; under TP, the latent is replicated on every rank.

baixo-posto.d: Writing an \( m \times n \) matrix as the product of two thinner ones, \( A\,(m\times r) \) and \( B\,(r\times n) \), with a small \( r \): \( r(m+n) \) numbers instead of \( mn \), and everything passes through an \( r \)-dimensional bottleneck. The basis of MLA (q_lora_rank, kv_lora_rank, o_lora_rank) and of LoRA.

latente-kv.d: Low-dimensional vector \( c^{KV}_t = W^{DKV} x_t \) (512 dims), computed per token in an MLA layer. It is the only content stored in the KV cache (plus the RoPE key, when there is decoupled RoPE); the keys and values of the heads are linear functions of it.

projecao-de-descida.d: First half of a low-rank factorization: it takes the token state down into the bottleneck. In MLA: kv_a_proj_with_mqa (\( W^{DKV} \)) and q_a_proj (\( W^{DQ} \)); in DeepSeek-V4, wkv and wq_a.

projecao-de-subida.d: Second half of the factorization: it takes the latent up to the space of each head. In MLA, kv_b_proj stacks \( W^{UK} \) and \( W^{UV} \), and q_b_proj is \( W^{UQ} \). During decode, \( W^{UK} \) and \( W^{UV} \) are absorbed into the query and the output.

kv-lora-rank.d: Dimension of the MLA KV latent (\( d_c \)): 512 in DeepSeek-V2/V3 and in GLM-5.3-Flash. In DeepSeek-V4, vLLM uses kv_lora_rank = head_dim = 512, because the latent is the key and the value itself. It is part of the checkpoint, not a recipe knob.

q-lora-rank.d: Dimension of the query bottleneck in MLA (\( d'_c \)): q_a_proj/wq_a → norm → q_b_proj/wq_b. 1536 in GLM and DeepSeek-V3, 1024 in DeepSeek-V4. It saves parameters and weight bandwidth, not KV.

o-lora-rank.d: In DeepSeek-V4, the output width of each wo_a[g] projection of the grouped output (1024). With 8 groups, the concatenation has 8,192 dimensions and goes through wo_b down to 4096.

o-groups.d: In DeepSeek-V4, the 64 heads form 8 groups of 8. Each group goes through wo_a (4096 → 1024, a BMM with \( r = 8 \times 512 = 4096 \)) and the concatenation through wo_b (8192 → 4096): half the parameters of a direct projection. The \( r = 4096 \) contract forces TP=3 to pad groups (8 → 9), not heads.

absorcao-de-pesos.d: Using the associativity \( q^\top(W^{UK}c) = (W^{UK\top}q)^\top c \) to bring the query into latent space and attend directly over the latents in the cache, applying \( W^{UV} \) only after the sum. It avoids rebuilding past K and V at every step; that is why kv_b_proj is read directly and stays in BF16 in the recipes.

kv-b-proj.d: MLA up-projection (DeepSeek-V2/V3, GLM): it stacks \( W^{UK} \) and \( W^{UV} \) for all heads (GLM: [32768, 512] = 64 × (256 + 256)). Since absorption reads the tensor directly, the recipes do not quantize it: dense FP8 and EXL3 both leave it in BF16.

rope-desacoplado.d: DeepSeek-V2's solution for reconciling RoPE with absorption: position goes into a small, separate part of the head (64 dims), with a RoPE key shared by all heads and stored next to the latent. Hence the 576 = 512 + 64 geometry of MLA kernels.

geometria-de-kernel.d: Set of shapes fixed when a kernel is compiled: key dimension, bytes per cache row, top-k, local heads, page size. FlashInfer SM120 instantiates DSV3_2 and GLM_NSA (576, 656 B) and DSV4 (512, 584 B); a model outside them needs padding or a new kernel.

rope-pad.d: GLM recipe build patch: when qk_rope_head_dim == 0 (and kv_lora_rank == 512), it appends 64 zeros to the query and writes k_pe as zeros, dressing the NoPE MLA (512) in the 576 GLM_NSA geometry. It is exact and costs 656 B per token instead of ~528.

k-igual-v.d: In DeepSeek-V4, a single 512-dim vector per token and layer (448 NoPE + 64 RoPE) serves as key and value for all 64 heads (num_key_value_heads = 1). There are no up-projections: what is specific to each head lives in the query and the output, and the RoPE part of the value requires inverse RoPE on the output.

fused-inv-rope.d: DeepSeek-V4 kernel in vLLM that applies inverse RoPE (position \( -i \)) to the 64 RoPE dims of the attention output and quantizes it to FP8 on the spot for the grouped einsum of wo_a. It requires, per rank, num_heads == n_groups × heads_per_group.
